title: Geometric stalks of structure-module etale sum extension
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $j:Z\to X$ be a representable etale morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $M$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $j_!M$ be module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the presheaf on etale scheme objects $W\to X$ given by $\bigoplus_{a:W\to Z\text{ over }X}M(W,a)$, with restrictions sending the $a$-summand to the restricted lift summand. For a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, stalks are colimits over pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods. For each lift $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z$ with $j\bar z=\bar x$, the structural map $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}\to\mathcal O_{Z,\bar z}$ is an isomorphism. Regarding $M_{\bar z}$ as an $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$-module through this map, there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$(j_!M)_{\bar x}\cong\bigoplus_{\bar z:\,j\bar z=\bar x}M_{\bar z}.$$
For a pointed etale scheme neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar x$, a lift $a:W\to Z$, and $m\in M(W,a)$, this isomorphism sends the germ of $m$ in the $a$-summand to the germ of $m$ in the summand indexed by $a\bar w$. This formula is natural in $M$. No finiteness or nonemptiness of the set of lifts, separation, or quasi-compactness is assumed.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], etale $j$ is localization of ringed sites, so $j^{-1}\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Z$ with the canonical structural identification. Apply [lem-sfb-space-geometric-points-conservative] to $j$ and the ring sheaf $\mathcal O_X$: $(j^{-1}\mathcal O_X)_{\bar z}\cong\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ compatibly with the canonical stalk-ring map and ring operations. Consequently that structural map $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}\to\mathcal O_{Z,\bar z}$ is an isomorphism. Use it throughout to restrict the scalars of $M_{\bar z}$ to $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$.

source.place: Tag 0710 (lemma-stalk-j-shriek), proof on representatives; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 08GU (equation-stalk-j-shriek) and preceding equation-stalk-restriction.

proof.text: Write $P(W)=\bigoplus_{a:W\to Z/X}M(W,a)$ for the presheaf in the statement. Every such $a$ is etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], since $W$ and $Z$ are etale over $X$. Its summands therefore are values on the small etale site of $Z$. Restrictions are semilinear and satisfy the presheaf identities by those of $M$, including when several lift summands merge. The category of pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods is small and cofiltered by [lem-sfb-space-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]. Coverings lift their geometric point by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift], applied to the covering of the scheme $W$. Hence $u(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(\bar x,W)$ satisfies the site-point axioms of [lem-sfb-site-point-abelian-sheafification-fibre]. That lemma applied to the underlying abelian presheaf gives $P_{\bar x}\cong(j_!M)_{\bar x}$, induced by sheafification. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] the unit is module-linear, so its stalk is linear over $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ as well.

proof.text: For $(W,\bar w)$ define an additive map $P(W)\to\bigoplus_{j\bar z=\bar x}M_{\bar z}$ on the $a$-summand by $m\mapsto\iota_{a\bar w}[W,a,\bar w,m]$. Restricting along a pointed arrow $r:(V,\bar v)\to(W,\bar w)$ changes $a$ to $ar$ and $m$ to $m|_V$, but $(ar)\bar v=a\bar w$ and these sections have the same germ in $M_{a\bar w}$. Thus the maps are compatible, also for sums with merged indices. The colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives a homomorphism $\Phi:P_{\bar x}\to\bigoplus_{j\bar z=\bar x}M_{\bar z}$.

source.place: Tag 0710 (lemma-stalk-j-shriek), proof on representatives; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 08GU (equation-stalk-j-shriek) and preceding equation-stalk-restriction.

proof.text: Fix a lift $\bar z$. For every pointed etale scheme neighbourhood $(V\xrightarrow{b}Z,\bar v)$ of $\bar z$, composition with $j$ is an etale scheme neighbourhood of $\bar x$ by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Send $m\in M(V,b)$ to its $b$-summand in $P(V)$ and then to $P_{\bar x}$. This is compatible with every pointed arrow over $Z$, by the defining restrictions of $P$. The colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $\Psi_{\bar z}:M_{\bar z}\to P_{\bar x}$. Taking the sum of these homomorphisms gives $\Psi:\bigoplus_{j\bar z=\bar x}M_{\bar z}\to P_{\bar x}$.

source.place: Tag 0710 (lemma-stalk-j-shriek), proof on representatives; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 08GU (equation-stalk-j-shriek) and preceding equation-stalk-restriction.

proof.text: On the germ of a section $m\in M(W,a)$ in an $a$-summand, $\Psi\Phi$ returns precisely that germ in $P_{\bar x}$. On a section germ in the $\bar z$-summand, $\Phi\Psi$ returns precisely the same germ in that summand. These identities imply identities of the homomorphisms: maps out of a colimit are determined on its cocone maps [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and maps out of a direct sum are determined on its summands. For linearity, represent a scalar germ and a section germ on one common pointed neighbourhood, using cofilteredness [lem-sfb-space-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]; every germ has a section representative by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] with $R=\mathbf Z$ on the underlying abelian diagrams. On that neighbourhood the formula for $\Phi$ commutes with multiplication by the scalar, by the module germ action and the stalk-ring identifications of step 1. Thus $\Phi$, and hence its inverse, are $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$-linear. A module map $M\to N$ commutes with each section-to-germ map, so the same formula commutes with it on every summand, proving naturality. Combining with step 2 gives the stated isomorphism and its exact germ formula. Empty sets of lifts give the zero direct sum; arbitrary lift sets cause no problem because every section of a direct sum has finite support.
